tools.name: search_events
tools.description:
Search BORME registry events (since 2009) across companies by publication
date, province, act type and company name, newest first.

Use it for questions about many companies ("insolvency notices in Valencia
in September"). For one known company use company_history; to find a
company use search_compa

tools.name: company_history
tools.description:
Get one company's BORME timeline: its published registry events within your
plan's window.

Use it once the company is known (a slug from search_companies or
company_by_nif); across many companies use search_events. A name is
searched too: several matches return {ambiguous: true, candidates}, none
r

tools.name: company_snapshot
tools.description:
Get one company's current registry card: the same answer as the REST API's
GET /v1/companies/{slug}.

Use it for "who runs it, who owns it, what capital": officers (the current
roles derived from the published acts), sole_shareholder as printed,
capital_eur, address, status, NIF with its source, pub

tools.name: company_signals
tools.description:
Get one company's derived signals within your plan's window, newest first:
the REST API's GET /v1/companies/{slug}/signals.

Use it for one company's ownership changes, mass exits, insolvency
declarations and the like; across all companies use recent_signals. A name
is searched as in
company_history

tools.name: company_by_nif
tools.description:
Look up a Spanish company by its NIF/CIF tax ID. Use it when the user gives
a tax ID (with a name use search_companies); on a hit, call
company_history with company_slug.

Returns JSON {found, company_slug, current_name, status, nif_source,
nif_caveat, ...}; use current_name. BORME has no dedicated

tools.name: brand_owner
tools.description:
Find the Spanish company a trademark or trading name is linked to, in the
Spanish patent office's (OEPM) trademark and commercial-name records we
hold (the archive starts in 1987).

Use it when the user names a brand; for a company's own name use
search_companies, for a known company's brands use co

tools.name: company_brands
tools.description:
List the trademarks and trading names that the Spanish patent office (OEPM)
records under a holder with this company's name.

Use it for a known company (a slug from search_companies or
company_history); to go from a brand to its company use brand_owner.

Returns JSON {company_slug, commercial_names

tools.name: recent_signals
tools.description:
Get a sample of the latest risk signals derived from BORME and public
sources: at most 10 rows dated within the last 7 days.

Use it for "what risk signals appeared this week"; not a per-company check
(use company_history) and not the full feed (the hosted API's
/v1/signals).

Returns JSON {count, w

tools.name: daily_digest
tools.description:
Summarise one BORME publication day: total events, counts by act type, the
top 10 provinces and the day's insolvency-proceedings notices.

Use it for "what was published today" or a day's figures; to read the
notices use search_events with date_from = date_to = that day.

Returns JSON {date, total_e

tools.name: act_stats
tools.description:
Count BORME acts by act type, period (month, quarter or year) and
province: how many companies and entries had mergers, spin-offs, capital
increases or any other act type, newest period first.

Use it for trends ("mergers per quarter in Spain since 2020"). To read
the acts themselves use search_even

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description:
Find Spanish companies by name and return ranked company cards. Use it first
when the user gives a company name, then company_history with its
company_slug; with a tax ID use company_by_nif, with a brand use
brand_owner.

Matches current names, former names and variants, ignoring accents, case,
punc

tools.name: list_act_types
tools.description:
List every normalized BORME act type: the enum used by the act_types filter
of search_events (act_type), its Spanish label (spanish) and its English
label (english).

Use it to choose act_types values or to translate act types in an answer; it
reads no registry data. Returns a JSON array of {act_typ

tools.name: registry_stats
tools.description:
Report the coverage and freshness of the BORME data behind this server.

Use it to answer "how much data is there?", "how fresh is it?" and "can I
trust date filters for period X?" before running searches; it says
nothing about any one company.

Returns JSON {events_approx, companies_approx, coverag

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: recent_signals · Private data: search_events, company_history, company_snapshot, company_by_nif, brand_owner, company_brands, recent_signals, daily_digest · Public sink: company_snapshot, company_by_nif, brand_owner, company_brands, recent_signals, daily_digest, act_stats · Destructive: registry_stats.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: recent_signals · Private data: search_events, company_history, company_snapshot, company_by_nif, brand_owner, company_brands, recent_signals, daily_digest · Public sink: company_snapshot, company_by_nif, brand_owner, company_brands, recent_signals, daily_digest, act_stats · Destructive: registry_stats

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
